name: Jeremiah
tagline: The weeping prophet and the new covenant
author: Jeremiah, with Baruch as scribe.
setting: The last decades of Judah and the fall of Jerusalem to Babylon.
theme: God judges persistent sin yet promises a new covenant written on the heart.

outline.label: Prophets in conflict and the letter to the exiles
The siege and the fall of Jerusalem
Egypt, Philistia, Moab, Ammon, Edom, and others

christInBook: Jeremiah, the weeping prophet who was rejected by his people, points to Christ, who wept over Jerusalem. The promise of a new covenant (31:31-34) is fulfilled in Jesus, who said, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood” (Luke 22:20).
howToRead: The book is not in chronological order. Read it as a collage of sermons, poems, stories, and visions. Notice Jeremiah’s personal laments, and look for the promise of a new covenant, the central hope of the book.
